Fixed. The bug was in `shardFor` (src/shard.ts:16): JavaScript's `%` is a truncated remainder that keeps the sign of the dividend, so any key whose FNV-1a hash came out negative (roughly half of all keys) produced a negative shard index — occasionally out of range and occasionally landing on a different shard than the routing table's Python-style non-negative modulo expected. That's why the range test in `test/shard.test.ts` failed intermittently depending on which random keys were generated. The test itself was correct.

Fix: normalize with `((hashKey(key) % shards) + shards) % shards` to always return the non-negative remainder, matching Python's `%` semantics as the comment already documented. Verified the suite passes three consecutive runs, the known negative-hash key now maps to the documented shards (13 of 16, 1 of 10), no test/fixture files changed, and `saga gate check` reports all gates met.
